# Wheat

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="wheat-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="wheat-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="wheat-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Wheat grain usually carries 20–70 µg/kg cadmium and little detectable lead, arsenic or mercury; cadmium is the metal to check, against EU limits of 100 µg/kg for common wheat and 180 µg/kg for durum.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Cadmium decides most wheat questions; nickel and chromium are higher in concentration, and lead is a concern mainly near contaminated sites.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li D, Zhang C, Li X, Li F, Liao S, Zhao Y, Wang Z, Sun D, Zhang Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Co-exposure of potentially toxic elements in wheat grains reveals a probabilistic health risk in Southwestern Guizhou, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anahita Moradi, Naser Honarjoo, Payam Najafi, Jaber Fallahzade · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

<a id="overview"></a>
<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Wheat overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Cadmium is the metal that decides most wheat questions. In WHO GEMS/Food, 10,625 common wheat grain results had a median of 28–29 µg/kg, and 4.2% were above the EU maximum of 100 µg/kg for common wheat; lead, total arsenic and total mercury medians sat below their reporting limits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Wheat contributes so much dietary cadmium because it is eaten in large amounts, not because its concentrations are unusually high: the joint FAO/WHO expert committee identified wheat as one of the main sources, at 3–29% of the tolerable intake across regional diets.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006">Evaluation of certain food contaminants — Sixty-fourth report of the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Technical Report Series 930 (Sixty-fourth meeting of JECFA, Rome, 8-17 February 2005)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Two comparisons matter more than any country ranking. Durum wheat, the hard wheat used for pasta, had a monitoring median of 70 µg/kg cadmium against 20 µg/kg for soft wheat reported by the same European programme, and the EU allows it a higher limit (180 against 100 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Within the kernel, cadmium concentrates in the outer and germ fractions: bran had a median of 64 µg/kg and germ 110 µg/kg, against 28–29 µg/kg in whole grain.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Grain from fields beside steel mills, battery plants and mines carried several times more cadmium and lead than grain from background farmland in the same studies.<sup class="cite">[[sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anahita Moradi, Naser Honarjoo, Payam Najafi, Jaber Fallahzade · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">A Human Health Risk Assessment of Soil and Crops Contaminated by Heavy Metals in Industrial Regions, Central Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Human and Ecological Risk Assessment: An International Journal (accepted manuscript, 29 Sep 2015)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Xu D, Shen Z, Dou C, Dou Z, Li Y, Gao Y, Sun Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals">Effects of soil properties on heavy metal bioavailability and accumulation in crop grains under different farmland use patterns</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jiang Y, Ma J, Ruan X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals">Compound health risk assessment of cumulative heavy metal exposure: A case study of a village near a battery factory in Henan Province, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science: Processes &amp; Impacts</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer, the supported priorities are a lot-specific cadmium result compared with the limit for the right wheat type (common, durum, bran or germ), a lead result, and knowledge of where and on what soil the grain was grown.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health <a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as wheat grain

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers wheat grain: common or bread wheat (Triticum aestivum), durum and other tetraploid wheats, the hulled wheats spelt, einkorn and emmer, and the bran and germ milled from them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a <p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one subgroup, material and metal; a mean and a range from the same samples are separate rows. Ratings place a reported mean, median or sample result against a pooled HMI wheat reference for the same material and basis, built from every compatible sampling family. Same-study contrasts compare an origin, cultivar, site or fraction with its own study’s reference group. Held rows failed a check against their own paper and are shown but not compared.</p>

methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:wheat-grain-dry-Cd:f7d3e95d0592"><summary>HMI wheat reference: wheat grain, dry weight, Cd · 3 sampling families</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:wheat-grain-dry-Cd:f7d3e95d0592"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI wheat reference: wheat grain, dry weight, Cd · 3 sampling families. Dry weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>124</td><td>124</td><td>175</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>124</td><td>124</td><td>175</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>11 reference units; 3 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>2</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Alemu et al. 2022</td><td>8</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Li et al. 2022</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians from every compatible wheat grain sampling family in the evidence ledger on a dry weight basis: WHO GEMS/Food region-by-year medians (random sampling only), published subgroup medians and per-sample or per-variety results. Each family has equal total weight; subgroups have equal weight within a family. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Dry-weight and as-sold results form separate references, and grain from point-source contaminated sites is compared within its own study but does not set the reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1–Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>An international evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world wheat market. GEMS/Food regions are reporting regions, not growing origins. Many submissions are non-detects with differing limits, which widens the bounds. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach wheat grain

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

Point sources and naturally high-cadmium soils both matter. Near a steel mill in Isfahan, grain carried 280–310 µg/kg cadmium and 2,000–2,100 µg/kg lead against 60 and 290 µg/kg at a background site, and grain from a village beside a battery factory in Henan had 320 µg/kg cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anahita Moradi, Naser Honarjoo, Payam Najafi, Jaber Fallahzade · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">A Human Health Risk Assessment of Soil and Crops Contaminated by Heavy Metals in Industrial Regions, Central Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Human and Ecological Risk Assessment: An International Journal (accepted manuscript, 29 Sep 2015)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jiang Y, Ma J, Ruan X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals">Compound health risk assessment of cumulative heavy metal exposure: A case study of a village near a battery factory in Henan Province, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science: Processes &amp; Among imported durum lots sampled in Italy in 2015–2020, cadmium medians were lowest for grain grown in Australia (8.5 µg/kg, 4 lots) and Turkey (17 µg/kg, 10 lots), then Russia (20 µg/kg, 105 lots) and Kazakhstan (25 µg/kg, 151 lots), and highest for Canada (54 µg/kg, 51 lots) and the United States (94 µg/kg, 25 lots).<sup class="cite">[[sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Pompa C, D&#39;Amore T, Miedico O, Preite C, Chiaravalle AE · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Evaluation and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Selected Toxic Trace Elements in Durum Wheat (Triticum durum) Imported into the Italian Market: Six Years of Official Controls</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Russian and Kazakh lots are numerous enough to call tentatively lower than North American durum; <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-durum-wheat-higher-in-cadmium-than-common-wheat" data-anchor="is-durum-wheat-higher-in-cadmium-than-common-wheat" data-question="Is durum wheat higher in cadmium than common wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is durum wheat higher in cadmium than common wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, in the monitoring and genetic evidence: European durum grain had a cadmium median of 70 µg/kg against 20 µg/kg for soft wheat, and 21% of durum results exceeded 100 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most modern durum cultivars carry an HMA3 allele that raises cadmium transport to the grain two- to threefold, and the EU sets a higher durum limit of 180 µg/kg to reflect this.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a <summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which durum origins measured lowest in cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

At Italian border controls in 2015–2020, durum from Australia (median 8.5 µg/kg, 4 lots), Turkey (17), Russia (20) and Kazakhstan (25) was lower than durum from Canada (54) and the United States (94).<sup class="cite">[[sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Pompa C, D&#39;Amore T, Miedico O, Preite C, Chiaravalle AE · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Evaluation and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Selected Toxic Trace Elements in Durum Wheat (Triticum durum) Imported into the Italian Market: Six Years of Official Controls</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Turkish durum had the highest lead, so an origin chosen for cadmium should still be tested for lead.<sup class="cite">[[sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Pompa C, D&#39;Amore T, Miedico O, Preite C, Chiaravalle AE · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Evaluation and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Selected Toxic Trace Elements in Durum Wheat (Triticum durum) Imported into the Italian Market: Six Years of Official Controls</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-some-wheat-varieties-accumulate-less-cadmium" data-anchor="do-some-wheat-varieties-accumulate-less-cadmium" data-question="Do some wheat varieties accumulate less cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do some wheat varieties accumulate less cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes. Durum cultivars with the functional HMA3 allele accumulate less cadmium, Polish wheat (Triticum polonicum) was lower than durum and Khorasan wheat grown in the same Italian field, and Ethiopian varieties ranged from 47 to 199 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/maccaferri2019-durum-wheat-genome-cadmium|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span S, Bonarrigo M, Cammerata A, Quagliata G, Astolfi S, Lafiandra D, Sestili F, Masci S · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/palombieri2023-triticum-turgidum-cadmium">Characterization <a id="processing-effects"></a>
<a id="ingredient-derivative-risk"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Milling fractions and processing

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Milling separates the bran and germ, where cadmium is concentrated, from the starchy endosperm that becomes white flour.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain on a request from the European Commission on cadmium in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Monitoring medians were 64 µg/kg for bran and 110 µg/kg for germ against 28–29 µg/kg for whole grain, and inorganic arsenic was also higher in bran (median 14–17 µg/kg) than in grain.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The European cadmium opinion likewise reported bran and germ at a mean of 64.7 µg/kg against 30.0 µg/kg for wheat grains and flour.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain on a request from the European Commission on cadmium in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A review citing durum milling studies reports that milling reduced nickel most, then arsenic, cadmium and lead, but gives no measured percentages.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2018-toxic-metals-like-arsenic-cadmium-and-lead-as|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2018-toxic-metals-like-arsenic-cadmium-and-lead-as">toxic metals like arsenic, cadmium and lead; as well as process contaminants such as acrylamide.</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2018-toxic-metals-like-arsenic-cadmium-and-lead-as">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Flour and finished foods are assessed on their own pages, so this page does not state how much cadmium a given flour retains.

No study in the library measured cleaning, sorting or washing of wheat grain against a control for metals. Roasting and crushing grain for soy sauce did not remove cadmium: the roasted, crushed wheat used in one Japanese brewing study still carried 57 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shindoh2010-cadmium-soy-sauce-miso-processing|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shindoh, Kumiko, Abe, Takashi, Yasui, Akemi · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shindoh2010-cadmium-soy-sauce-miso-processing">Changes in Cadmium Content when Processing Soybean to Miso and Soy Sauce</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Report of the National Food Research Institute (Rep. Nat&#39;l Food Res. Inst), No. 74</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shindoh2010-cadmium-soy-sauce-miso-processing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-removing-bran-and-germ-lower-cadmium" data-anchor="does-removing-bran-and-germ-lower-cadmium" data-question="Does removing bran and germ lower cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does removing bran and germ lower cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

It moves cadmium out of the main stream: bran (median 64 µg/kg) and germ (110 µg/kg) carry more than whole grain (28–29 µg/kg), so flour milled from the endosperm carries less than the grain it came from.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The removed bran and germ keep the cadmium, which is why the EU sets higher limits for them (150 and 200 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

Direction is shown separately. These are descriptive display bands, not validated efficacy cutoffs, occurrence-baseline positions, statistical significance, evidence certainty, safety or net benefit. A range spanning bands retains both labels; a qualitative label has no implied percentage.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Control in context</p><p>Excluding lots above a maximum level of 100 µg/kg would lower mean wheat cadmium by 22% (10% of samples excluded), against 6% at 200 µg/kg (1% excluded); the cut in highest intake was about 6% and 1% of the tolerable intake.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Context</th><th scope="col">Selected control</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Material</td><td>Wheat grain, international occurrence data</td></tr><tr><td>Stage</td><td>lot acceptance and release</td></tr><tr><td>Audience</td><td>Ingredient suppliers · Brands</td></tr><tr><td>Period</td><td>As reported</td></tr><tr><td>Conditions</td><td>Regulatory or buyer lot rejection.</td></tr><tr><td>Tested scale</td><td>Regulatory assessment</td></tr><tr><td>Sample units</td><td>Source sampling units; plots, pots or lots as stated.</td></tr><tr><td>Trade-offs</td><td>Other metals, yield and cost not quantified unless stated.</td></tr><tr><td>Verification</td><td>Confirm with lot-specific cadmium and lead results using an adequate quantification limit.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Design, applicability and operating conditions</p><p>Author guidance or regulatory assessment. Bread, pasta and other products made from wheat are measured on their own pages, and this page does not transfer grain concentrations to them. This assessment covers every source record in the HMI library that is tagged to wheat or names it, plus every wheat row in WHO GEMS/Food, the FDA Total Diet Study and other indexed datasets; each has a recorded decision based on its content. The FDA Total Diet Study has no wheat grain food, only bread, cereals, pasta, flour and cream of wheat, so it contributes no rows here. <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Wheat FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-wheat" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-wheat" data-question="What heavy metals are found in wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Cadmium is found in almost every wheat sample, typically 20–70 µg/kg depending on the wheat type, while lead, arsenic and mercury are usually below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Wheat also carries nickel and chromium in the hundreds of µg/kg, and aluminium in the thousands.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li D, Zhang C, Li X, Li F, Liao S, Zhao Y, Wang Z, Sun D, Zhang Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Co-exposure of potentially toxic elements in wheat grains reveals a probabilistic health risk in Southwestern Guizhou, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/stahl2017-aluminum-food-contact-part1|37]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Stahl T, Falk S, Rohrbeck A, Georgii S, Herzog C, Wiegand A, Hotz S, Boschek B, Zorn H, Brunn H · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/stahl2017-aluminum-food-contact-part1">Migration of aluminum from food contact materials to food - a health risk for consumers? Part I of III: exposure to aluminum, release of aluminum, tolerable weekly intake (TWI), toxicological effects of aluminum, study design, and methods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Sciences Europe</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/stahl2017-aluminum-food-contact-part1">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-wheat" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-wheat" data-question="How do heavy metals get into wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Through the roots, from soil and irrigation water; uptake rises with soil cadmium and falls as soil pH rises.<sup class="cite">[[sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Xu D, Shen Z, Dou C, Dou Z, Li Y, Gao Y, Sun Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals">Effects of soil properties on heavy metal bioavailability and accumulation in crop grains under different farmland use patterns</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Fields near steel mills, battery plants and mines give grain with several times more cadmium and lead than background farmland.<sup class="cite">[[sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anahita Moradi, Naser Honarjoo, Payam Najafi, Jaber Fallahzade · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">A Human Health Risk Assessment of Soil and Crops Contaminated by Heavy Metals in Industrial Regions, Central Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Human and Ecological Risk Assessment: An International Journal (accepted manuscript, 29 Sep 2015)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jiang Y, Ma J, Ruan X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals">Compound health risk assessment of cumulative heavy metal exposure: A case study of a village near a battery factory in Henan Province, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science: Processes &amp; Impacts</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-organic-wheat-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-anchor="is-organic-wheat-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-question="Is organic wheat lower in heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is organic wheat lower in heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library holds no reliable comparison of organic and conventional wheat grain. The one survey of ecological bran reported cadmium values that failed checks against the paper itself, so it cannot answer the question.<sup class="cite">[[sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland|35]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Slepecka K, Kalwa K, Wyrostek J, Pankiewicz U · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Evaluation of cadmium, lead, zinc and copper levels in selected ecological cereal food products and their non-ecological counterparts</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Current Issues in Pharmacy and Medical Sciences 30(3):147-150</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/slepecka2017-ecological-cereal-heavy-metals-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-wheat-have-the-lowest-cadmium" data-anchor="which-types-of-wheat-have-the-lowest-cadmium" data-question="Which types of wheat have the lowest cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of wheat have the lowest cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Common (soft) wheat and spelt measured lower than durum: European medians were 20 µg/kg for soft wheat, 31 for spelt, einkorn and emmer, and 70 for durum.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Within durum, cultivars with the functional HMA3 allele accumulate less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/maccaferri2019-durum-wheat-genome-cadmium|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Maccaferri M, Harris NS, Twardziok SO, Pasam RK, Gundlach H, Spannagl M, Ormanbekova D, Lux T, Prade VM, Milner SG, Himmelbach A, Mascher M, Bagnaresi P, Faccioli P, Cozzi P, Lauria M, Lazzari B, Stella A, Manconi A, Gnocchi M, Moscatelli M, Avanzati AM, Gualandi V, Palazzi P, Conti V, Del Prete G, Baldi P, Licciardello C, Tagliavia V, Cattivelli L, Ceccarelli S, Bogard M, Praud S, Rousseau-Gueutin M, Delobel F, Poncet C, Barabaschi D, Marone D, Laidò G, Mazzucotelli E, De Vita P, Mastrangelo AM, Pecchioni N, Nicosia OLD, Fiore MC, Porreca C, Frenna A, Venora G, Postiglione L, Gruszecka AM, Rhoné B, Simkova H, Dolezel J, Bhullar NK, Bailey M, Krasileva KV, Wang X, McNeil MD, Paux E, Keller B, Morgante M, Platzer M, Gundlach H · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/maccaferri2019-durum-wheat-genome-cadmium">A high-density, SNP-based consensus map of tetraploid wheat as a bridge to integrate durum and bread wheat genomics and breeding</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nature Genetics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/maccaferri2019-durum-wheat-genome-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-countries-grow-wheat-with-the-lowest-cadmium" data-anchor="which-countries-grow-wheat-with-the-lowest-cadmium" data-question="Which countries grow wheat with the lowest cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which countries grow wheat with the lowest cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For durum sampled at Italian border controls, Australia, Turkey, Russia and Kazakhstan were lower than Canada and the United States (medians 8.5–25 against 54–94 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Pompa C, D&#39;Amore T, Miedico O, Preite C, Chiaravalle AE · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Evaluation and Dietary Exposure Assessment of Selected Toxic Trace Elements in Durum Wheat (Triticum durum) Imported into the Italian Market: Six Years of Official Controls</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/pompa2021-durum-wheat-cd-pb-hg-italy">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For common wheat, monitoring data identify only reporting regions, not growing countries, so no country ranking is supported.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-bread-pasta-and-flour-made-from-wheat-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-anchor="do-bread-pasta-and-flour-made-from-wheat-also-contain-heavy-metals" data-question="Do bread, pasta and flour made from wheat also contain heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do bread, pasta and flour made from wheat also contain heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, but at concentrations set by milling and recipe: in the European cadmium opinion, bread and pasta averaged 13.7 µg/kg against 30.0 for wheat grains and flour.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain on a request from the European Commission on cadmium in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Each product is assessed on its own page from its own measurements.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-cadmium-levels-in-wheat-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-cadmium-levels-in-wheat-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the cadmium levels in wheat mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the cadmium levels in wheat mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Wheat is a major dietary source of cadmium because it is a staple: the joint FAO/WHO committee estimated it at 3–29% of the tolerable intake across regional diets.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006">Evaluation of certain food contaminants — Sixty-fourth report of the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Technical Report Series 930 (Sixty-fourth meeting of JECFA, Rome, 8-17 February 2005)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cadmium accumulates in the kidney over years, so the concern is long-term intake from staple foods rather than any single meal; occurrence data alone do not establish individual risk.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006">Evaluation of certain food contaminants — Sixty-fourth report of the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Technical Report Series 930 (Sixty-fourth meeting of JECFA, Rome, 8-17 February 2005)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-64th-cadmium-tin-2006">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-wheat" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-wheat" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes. The EU sets cadmium at 100 µg/kg for common wheat, 180 for durum, 150 for bran and 200 for germ, and lead at 200 µg/kg for cereals; Codex sets 0.2 mg/kg cadmium for wheat.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> China sets 0.1 mg/kg cadmium, 0.2 lead, 0.02 mercury, 0.5 total arsenic and 1.0 chromium for grain, and from July 2026 the EU limits nickel to 0.80 mg/kg in common wheat and 1.5 mg/kg in durum.<sup class="cite">[[sources/china2022-gb-2762-contaminants-original|30]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">National Health Commission of the People&#39;s Republic of China, State Administration for Market Regulation · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/china2022-gb-2762-contaminants-original">GB 2762-2022 National Food Safety Standard: Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">National Food Safety Standard GB 2762-2022</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/china2022-gb-2762-contaminants-original">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-milling-or-processing-reduce-heavy-metals-in-wheat" data-anchor="can-milling-or-processing-reduce-heavy-metals-in-wheat" data-question="Can milling or processing reduce heavy metals in wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can milling or processing reduce heavy metals in wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Milling separates the cadmium-rich bran and germ from the endosperm used for white flour, but it moves cadmium rather than destroying it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study in the library measured cleaning or washing grain against a control.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-the-arsenic-in-wheat-inorganic" data-anchor="is-the-arsenic-in-wheat-inorganic" data-question="Is the arsenic in wheat inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is the arsenic in wheat inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Wheat contains little arsenic of any form outside groundwater-arsenic regions: inorganic arsenic in monitored grain had a median of 2–9 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most European figures were estimated as 70% of total arsenic rather than measured, so a measured inorganic arsenic result is the better evidence.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|20]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-whole-wheat-contain-more-cadmium-than-white-wheat" data-anchor="does-whole-wheat-contain-more-cadmium-than-white-wheat" data-question="Does whole wheat contain more cadmium than white wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does whole wheat contain more cadmium than white wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Whole grain contains the bran and germ, which carry more cadmium (medians 64 and 110 µg/kg) than whole grain overall (28–29 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Products made from whole grain therefore keep more of the grain’s cadmium than refined flour does; flour itself is measured on the wheat flour page.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain on a request from the European Commission on cadmium in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-spelt-or-ancient-wheat-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-anchor="is-spelt-or-ancient-wheat-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-question="Is spelt or ancient wheat lower in heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is spelt or ancient wheat lower in heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For cadmium, spelt, einkorn and emmer grain had a monitoring median of 31 µg/kg, about the same as common wheat, and lower than durum.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A German laboratory found less aluminium in spelt (median 370 µg/kg) than in wheat (3,000 µg/kg), though the table does not say whether the samples were grain or milled.<sup class="cite">[[sources/stahl2017-aluminum-food-contact-part1|37]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Stahl T, Falk S, Rohrbeck A, Georgii S, Herzog C, Wiegand A, Hotz S, Boschek B, Zorn H, Brunn H · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/stahl2017-aluminum-food-contact-part1">Migration of aluminum from food contact materials to food - a health risk for consumers? Part I of III: exposure to aluminum, release of aluminum, tolerable weekly intake (TWI), toxicological effects of aluminum, study design, and methods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Sciences Europe</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/stahl2017-aluminum-food-contact-part1">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-often-does-wheat-exceed-the-eu-cadmium-limit" data-anchor="how-often-does-wheat-exceed-the-eu-cadmium-limit" data-question="How often does wheat exceed the EU cadmium limit?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How often does wheat exceed the EU cadmium limit?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In GEMS/Food, 4.2% of common wheat grain results exceeded 100 µg/kg, 1.1% of durum results exceeded 180, 1.7% of bran results exceeded 150 and 4.2% of germ results exceeded 200.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Exceedance was common in high-cadmium regions: 45% of wheat from Guizhou karst soils exceeded China’s 100 µg/kg limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2022-guizhou-cd-grains|22]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li X, Zhou L, Zhang C, Li D, Wang Z, Sun D, Liao C, Zhang Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2022-guizhou-cd-grains">Spatial distribution and risk assessment of fluorine and cadmium in rice, corn, and wheat grains in most karst regions of Guizhou province, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2022-guizhou-cd-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-zinc-fertiliser-lower-cadmium-in-wheat" data-anchor="does-zinc-fertiliser-lower-cadmium-in-wheat" data-question="Does zinc fertiliser lower cadmium in wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does zinc fertiliser lower cadmium in wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In a greenhouse trial with durum on cadmium-spiked soil, adequate soil zinc plus a foliar zinc spray gave the lowest grain cadmium at every cadmium dose.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ozkutlu2026-wheat-cd-zinc-mitigation|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ozkutlu F, Kocaman A, Ete Aydemir O · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ozkutlu2026-wheat-cd-zinc-mitigation">Roles of Soil and Foliar Spray of Zinc Nutrition in Cadmium Reduction of Wheat Grain</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">ACS Omega</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ozkutlu2026-wheat-cd-zinc-mitigation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> At the 0.2 mg/kg dose grain fell from 239 to 182 µg/kg, but zinc could not bring grain from more heavily spiked soil below 200 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ozkutlu2026-wheat-cd-zinc-mitigation|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ozkutlu F, Kocaman A, Ete Aydemir O · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ozkutlu2026-wheat-cd-zinc-mitigation">Roles of Soil and Foliar Spray of Zinc Nutrition in Cadmium Reduction of Wheat Grain</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">ACS Omega</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ozkutlu2026-wheat-cd-zinc-mitigation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-modern-wheat-varieties-carry-more-cadmium" data-anchor="do-modern-wheat-varieties-carry-more-cadmium" data-question="Do modern wheat varieties carry more cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do modern wheat varieties carry more cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In a Nebraska field trial of 18 hard winter wheat cultivars released between 1933 and 2013, newer cultivars carried slightly more cadmium, about 0.4 µg/kg per year of registration, without fungicide.<sup class="cite">[[sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Motta-Romero H, Niyongira F, Boehm JD Jr, Rose DJ · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide">Effects of foliar fungicide on yield, micronutrients, and cadmium in grains from historical and modern hard winter wheat genotypes</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For durum, the high-cadmium HMA3 allele is more common in modern cultivars (68%) than in landraces (26%).<sup class="cite">[[sources/maccaferri2019-durum-wheat-genome-cadmium|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Maccaferri M, Harris NS, Twardziok SO, Pasam RK, Gundlach H, Spannagl M, Ormanbekova D, Lux T, Prade VM, Milner SG, Himmelbach A, Mascher M, Bagnaresi P, Faccioli P, Cozzi P, Lauria M, Lazzari B, Stella A, Manconi A, Gnocchi M, Moscatelli M, Avanzati AM, Gualandi V, Palazzi P, Conti V, Del Prete G, Baldi P, Licciardello C, Tagliavia V, Cattivelli L, Ceccarelli S, Bogard M, Praud S, Rousseau-Gueutin M, Delobel F, Poncet C, Barabaschi D, Marone D, Laidò G, Mazzucotelli E, De Vita P, Mastrangelo AM, Pecchioni N, Nicosia OLD, Fiore MC, Porreca C, Frenna A, Venora G, Postiglione L, Gruszecka AM, Rhoné B, Simkova H, Dolezel J, Bhullar NK, Bailey M, Krasileva KV, Wang X, McNeil MD, Paux E, Keller B, Morgante M, Platzer M, Gundlach H · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/maccaferri2019-durum-wheat-genome-cadmium">A high-density, SNP-based consensus map of tetraploid wheat as a bridge to integrate durum and bread wheat genomics and breeding</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nature Genetics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/maccaferri2019-durum-wheat-genome-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-fungicide-affect-cadmium-in-wheat" data-anchor="does-fungicide-affect-cadmium-in-wheat" data-question="Does fungicide affect cadmium in wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does fungicide affect cadmium in wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the same Nebraska trial, a single fungicide application at booting lowered the range of cultivar cadmium means from 100–190 to 70–140 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Motta-Romero H, Niyongira F, Boehm JD Jr, Rose DJ · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide">Effects of foliar fungicide on yield, micronutrients, and cadmium in grains from historical and modern hard winter wheat genotypes</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The authors attribute this to larger yields diluting cadmium and caution that other fungicide chemistries were not tested.<sup class="cite">[[sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Motta-Romero H, Niyongira F, Boehm JD Jr, Rose DJ · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide">Effects of foliar fungicide on yield, micronutrients, and cadmium in grains from historical and modern hard winter wheat genotypes</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/motta-romero2021-wheat-cadmium-fungicide">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-wheat-grown-near-mines-or-factories-have-more-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-wheat-grown-near-mines-or-factories-have-more-heavy-metals" data-question="Does wheat grown near mines or factories have more heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does wheat grown near mines or factories have more heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, in every such study here: grain near a steel mill in Isfahan had 280–310 µg/kg cadmium and 2,000–2,100 µg/kg lead against 60 and 290 at a background site.<sup class="cite">[[sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Anahita Moradi, Naser Honarjoo, Payam Najafi, Jaber Fallahzade · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">A Human Health Risk Assessment of Soil and Crops Contaminated by Heavy Metals in Industrial Regions, Central Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Human and Ecological Risk Assessment: An International Journal (accepted manuscript, 29 Sep 2015)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/moradi2015-iran-isfahan-soil-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Grain beside a battery factory in Henan had 320 µg/kg cadmium, and 24 of 25 fields in a Chinese copper mining area exceeded 100 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Xu D, Shen Z, Dou C, Dou Z, Li Y, Gao Y, Sun Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals">Effects of soil properties on heavy metal bioavailability and accumulation in crop grains under different farmland use patterns</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/xu2022-crop-grains-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jiang Y, Ma J, Ruan X · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals">Compound health risk assessment of cumulative heavy metal exposure: A case study of a village near a battery factory in Henan Province, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science: Processes &amp; Impacts</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jiang2020-henan-battery-factory-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-nickel-a-concern-in-wheat" data-anchor="is-nickel-a-concern-in-wheat" data-question="Is nickel a concern in wheat?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is nickel a concern in wheat?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Wheat grain carries hundreds of µg/kg of nickel: 330 µg/kg on average in an early Nordic compilation and a median of 468 µg/kg in Bijie, Guizhou.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li D, Zhang C, Li X, Li F, Liao S, Zhao Y, Wang Z, Sun D, Zhang Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Co-exposure of potentially toxic elements in wheat grains reveals a probabilistic health risk in Southwestern Guizhou, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/flyvholm1984-nickel-content-food-dietary-intake|38]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mari-Ann Flyvholm, Gitte Dalsgaard Nielsen, Allan Andersen · 1984</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/flyvholm1984-nickel-content-food-dietary-intake">Nickel Content of Food and Estimation of Dietary Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Zeitschrift für Lebensmittel-Untersuchung und -Forschung 179(6):427-431</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/flyvholm1984-nickel-content-food-dietary-intake">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> From July 2026 the EU sets nickel limits of 0.80 mg/kg for common wheat and 1.5 mg/kg for durum, and the Bijie maximum (5,034 µg/kg) shows that some grain exceeds them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li D, Zhang C, Li X, Li F, Liao S, Zhao Y, Wang Z, Sun D, Zhang Q · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Co-exposure of potentially toxic elements in wheat grains reveals a probabilistic health risk in Southwestern Guizhou, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2022-wheat-pte-guizhou-health-risk">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-wheat-bran-or-wheat-germ-higher-in-metals" data-anchor="is-wheat-bran-or-wheat-germ-higher-in-metals" data-question="Is wheat bran or wheat germ higher in metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is wheat bran or wheat germ higher in metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Germ was higher in cadmium than bran in monitoring data (median 110 against 64 µg/kg), and both were higher than whole grain.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For inorganic arsenic, bran (median 14–17 µg/kg) was higher than grain; too few germ results exist to compare.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
